Zisik [=?] gives the following ph [=Eretz-Yisrael Hebrew (modern)] names: P. Lentiscus L. שיח לוט (after B. r. [=Bereshit Rabba, ed. Theodor and Albeck] 91, 11). P. Palaestina Boiss. אֵלָה (arab. [=Arabic] buṭm); P. mutica Fisch. et Mey. בטמה; P. vera L. בטנה (arab. fistuḳ) (Hasade 6, 206).
1. Pistacia Terebinthus L. Terebinth; turpentine tree.

Terebinth, merges by imperceptible gradations into var. Palaestina Engl., who is more common in our district then type. Rocky places and hillsides (Post [=Post, Flora of Syria, Palestine and Sinai] 206. Bornm. [=Bornmüller, Ein Beitrag zur Kenntnis der Flora von Syrien und Palästina] 30). The terebinth, buṭum, is the characteristic tree of the highlands, under whose mighty crown one gladly rests in the shade (Musil [=Musil, Arabia Petraea] 3, 15). The tree, incidentally, is not without exception evergreen (Fonck [=Fonck, Streifzüge durch die biblische Flora] 48). The terebinth is not very common in the mountains of Judah, but it is found west of Nazareth in the forest and in the Carmel woodlands (ZDPV. 8, 104. 108. 110).
